- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.17) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) or volatile, model often overshoots after spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent highs; apply mean reversion: if forecast > 20% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 10–20% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.11), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to catch momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price range; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to lower bound if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless strong bullish sentiment persists.
